RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel is weak evidence by itself — it shows who was available, not what they decided. In many jurisdictions, though, public-sector panels are expected to be gender-balanced, so the composition may be a procedural breach worth noting regardless of outcome.

Lead with the stronger points instead: your request for written reasons is overdue (chase it in writing, citing any statutory deadline), and on paper you hold the stronger formal qualifications. The decisive question is whether "experience of leading international projects" was in the published criteria or appeared afterwards — if it surfaced late, that's your real argument.

Mention the panel as context, not as your central claim. It weakens a case if it carries the weight alone.
